title: What Does It Mean To Seek The Lord
paragraphs: Understanding What It Means to Seek the Lord

The phrase “seek the Lord” appears throughout Scripture, calling God's people to pursue Him with their whole hearts. But what does it truly mean to seek the Lord? Is it a one-time act, a lifelong pursuit, or something else entirely? This study will explore the biblical foundation, practical implications, and the promises associated with seeking the Lord.
Biblical Foundations for Seeking the Lord

To seek the Lord is to earnestly desire His presence, guidance, and will above all else. It involves a conscious turning toward God, motivated by faith and humility. The Bible frequently encourages this pursuit:
Seek ye Jehovah while he may be found; call ye upon him while he is near: - Isaiah 55:6 ASV
But seek ye first his kingdom, and his righteousness; and all these things shall be added unto you. - Matthew 6:33 ASV
In both the Old and New Testaments, seeking the Lord is portrayed as an intentional act—an orientation of the heart and mind toward God.
How Do We Seek the Lord?
The Bible provides several practical steps and attitudes for seeking God:
Through Prayer: Coming before God in humble dependence, confessing our need, and expressing our longing for Him.
Call unto me, and I will answer thee, and will show thee great things, and difficult, which thou knowest not. - Jeremiah 33:3 ASV
Through God's Word: Diligently studying Scripture to know God’s character, promises, and commands.
Blessed are they that keep his testimonies, that seek him with the whole heart. - Psalm 119:2 ASV
With a Whole Heart: Seeking God requires sincerity, not mere outward actions.
And ye shall seek me, and find me, when ye shall search for me with all your heart. - Jeremiah 29:13 ASV
By Turning from Sin: Seeking the Lord involves repentance and a willingness to forsake sinful ways.

If my people, which are called by my name, shall humble themselves, and pray, and seek my face, and turn from their wicked ways; then will I hear from heaven, and will forgive their sin, and will heal their land. - 2 Chronicles 7:14 ASV
The Promises for Those Who Seek the Lord
Scripture is abundantly clear that God rewards those who earnestly seek Him. This pursuit is not in vain:
But without faith it is impossible to be well-pleasing unto him; for he that cometh to God must believe that he is, and that he is a rewarder of them that seek after him. - Hebrews 11:6 ASV
Draw nigh to God, and he will draw nigh to you. - James 4:8 ASV
Those who seek the Lord experience deeper fellowship with Him, increased wisdom, guidance in life’s decisions, and peace that surpasses understanding.
The Centrality of Christ in Seeking the Lord

Ultimately, seeking the Lord finds its fulfillment in seeking Jesus Christ Himself. He is the way to the Father (John 14:6 ASV) and the only mediator between God and humanity. Scripture calls us to fix our eyes on Christ:
Looking unto Jesus the author and perfecter of our faith. - Hebrews 12:2 ASV
To seek the Lord is, therefore, to trust in Christ for salvation, to follow Him in obedience, and to commune with Him daily.
Conclusion

Seeking the Lord is an ongoing, wholehearted pursuit that involves prayer, studying Scripture, repentance, and faith in Christ. It is not merely a duty but a privilege, rooted in the assurance that God desires to be found by those who earnestly seek Him.
